title: Linearity of finite-coefficient compact-support cohomology
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of the finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme with structure morphism $a_Y:Y\to s$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the finite-coefficient derived categories [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and the compact-support cohomology functor of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology],
$$
F_Y=R\Gamma_c(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}-):D^b_c(Y,A)\longrightarrow D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A).
$$
Then $F_Y$ is $A$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. Explicitly, for every $K,L\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, parallel morphisms $f,g:K\to L$, and $a\in A$, its map on morphisms satisfies
$$
F_Y(f+ag)=F_Y(f)+aF_Y(g)
$$
in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(F_YK,F_YL)$, with the usual scalar actions induced by the constant coefficient ring $A$.

source.place: Proof, the assertion of A-linearity of compact-support cohomology used for the middle arrow; its finite-coefficient conventions are def-trf-coefficient-conventions.

proof.text: By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $F_Y=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{Y!}$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is termwise $\Gamma(s,-)$ on the finite-coefficient category. Use the compactification $c=(j:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,\overline a:\overline Y\to s)$ chosen in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Its candidate [def-weil-compact-support-candidate] is $Ra_{Y!}^c=R\overline a_*\circ j_!$, where $j_!$ on derived categories is induced by its exact sheaf functor. We prove linearity on the ambient derived morphisms for this chosen candidate, then restrict to the full bounded constructible subcategory in the statement.

source.place: Middle-arrow compact-support linearity assertion, expanded using the defining compactification composite.

proof.text: For a sheaf of $A_T$-modules, multiplication by $a\in A$ means multiplication by its constant section on each site object. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sums of module-sheaf maps and scalar multiples are computed sectionwise; restrictions respect the constant sections. The module identities and bilinearity of composition are therefore the sectionwise identities for modules, giving the $A$-linear category of [def-weil-linear-category]. The category of $A$-modules has the same structure. Apply [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] to these abelian categories, in the site universes of the definitions: the ambient derived categories and their localization functors $Q$ are $A$-linear. In particular $Q(\alpha+a\beta)=Q\alpha+aQ\beta$, and composition with any fixed derived isomorphisms is $A$-linear by bilinearity. This is the scalar action of the statement, since $Q(a\operatorname{id}_C)=a\operatorname{id}_{QC}$.

source.place: Lines 24-36: linear derived categories and linear localization; constant-section specialization written here.

proof.text: The extension-by-zero presheaf construction in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] sends $u+av$ to $P(u)+aP(v)$: on a site object factoring through $j$ this is the original sectionwise identity, and on every other object both sides are zero. Write $\iota_M:P_M\to P_M^\#$ for sheafification. The two module-sheaf maps $j_!(u+av)$ and $j_!u+a j_!v$ have the same composite with $\iota_M$, by this presheaf identity and naturality of $\iota$. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] makes them equal. Thus the sheaf functor $j_!$ is $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules: uniqueness of factoring maps; the two-case presheaf calculation is written here.

proof.text: We check the induced functors of $j_!$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ on arbitrary derived morphisms. Both are exact: for $j_!$ this is part of [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], and for $\Gamma(s,-)$ it is stated in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. They are $A$-linear on sheaves, for $j_!$ by Step 3 and for $\Gamma(s,-)$ because $(u+av)_s=u_s+a v_s$. Choose K-injective resolutions $C\to I$, $D\to J$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For either functor $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents any two derived maps between $QI$ and $QJ$ by homotopy classes of chain maps $\alpha,\beta:I\to J$. Step 2 shows that their sum with scalar $a$ is represented by $\alpha+a\beta$. Since the induced exact functor satisfies $T_D(Q\alpha)=Q(T\alpha)$, degreewise linearity gives $T_D(Q(\alpha+a\beta))=Q(T\alpha+aT\beta)=Q(T\alpha)+aQ(T\beta)$. For the original objects, compose this equality with $T_D(Q(C\to I))$ and $T_D(Q(D\to J))^{-1}$; bilinearity from Step 2 gives the same equality on $\operatorname{Hom}(QC,QD)$. Thus both derived $j_!$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ are $A$-linear. This uses no assertion that a chosen resolution functor is itself linear.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clause (3); existence is injectives.tex Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck, via the cited site-module resolution node. The linearity calculation is written here.

proof.text: For the sheaf direct image $G=\overline a_*$, [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] gives $(G M)(V)=M(V\times_s\overline Y)$ and $(G u)_V=u_{V\times_s\overline Y}$. Its coefficient map takes a constant section $a$ to the constant section $a$. Consequently $(G(u+av))_V=u_{V\times_s\overline Y}+a v_{V\times_s\overline Y}=(Gu+aGv)_V$ on every site object $V$. Thus $G$ and its degreewise action on chain maps are $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward, clause (1), specialized to the constant coefficient ring and the sectionwise direct image of the cited node.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-derived-direct-image], $R\overline a_*=RG$ is computed with K-injectives. Take K-injective resolutions $C\to I$, $D\to J$ as supplied by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and let $\alpha,\beta:I\to J$ represent two derived maps using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the natural derived-functor comparison gives fixed isomorphisms $\eta_I:Q(GI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(QI)$ and $\eta_J:Q(GJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(QJ)$. Naturality gives $RG(Q\alpha)=\eta_J\circ Q(G\alpha)\circ\eta_I^{-1}$, also for $\beta$ and $\alpha+a\beta$. Step 5 and Step 2 therefore give
$$
RG(Q\alpha+aQ\beta)=\eta_J\circ Q(G\alpha+aG\beta)\circ\eta_I^{-1}=RG(Q\alpha)+aRG(Q\beta).
$$
For maps $h,t:QC\to QD$, replace them by $Q(D\to J)\circ h\circ Q(C\to I)^{-1}$ and the expression with $t$; composing the displayed equality with $RG(Q(D\to J))^{-1}$ on the left and $RG(Q(C\to I))$ on the right proves $RG(h+at)=RG(h)+aRG(t)$. Thus the derived direct image is $A$-linear without any assumption that $j_!$ preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, and the K-injective derived-functor comparison specified by def-sfb-right-derived-functor; injectives.tex Tag 079P supplies the resolutions. Naturality and the scalar calculation are written here.

proof.text:
For $f,g:K\to L$ in the full category $D^b_c(Y,A)$, apply Steps 4 and 6 to the composite of Step 1:
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_Y(f+ag)&=\operatorname{Fib}_s\bigl(R\overline a_*\bigl(j_!f+a j_!g\bigr)\bigr)\\
&=\operatorname{Fib}_s\bigl(R\overline a_*j_!f+aR\overline a_*j_!g\bigr)\\
&=F_Y(f)+aF_Y(g).
\end{aligned}
$$
The full-subcategory convention of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] leaves these Hom groups and scalar actions unchanged; the target is the functor already defined in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Taking $a=1$ proves additivity; taking $f=g=0$ and $a=1$ proves preservation of zero; then taking $f=0$ proves preservation of scalar multiples. These are exactly the conditions of [def-weil-linear-functor].

(2) The sectionwise A-linear structure plus the Mathlib leaf DerivedCategory.instLinear make D and Q A-linear. (3) j_! is linear on sheaves by the two-case presheaf identity and uniqueness of sheafification; genuinely elementary. (4) The exact functors j_! and Γ(s,−) are linear on derived Homs: resolutions from prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist (the site is V-small, as the size convention gives), and maps into K-injectives are represented by chain maps (Qh_map_bijective leaf), then conjugated by the resolution isomorphisms. (6) RG(Qα)=η_J Q(Gα) η_I^{-1}, using the unit of def-sfb-right-derived-functor, which is an isomorphism on K-injectives; correct, and needs no preservation of K-injectives. (7) The composite and restriction to full subcategories give def-weil-linear-functor. Edge cases Y=∅, Y=s, a=0 and 1, n=1 and n>1 pass.
